source: 4-loop equal-mass banana, asymmetric ISP basis (psq, msq).  First L=4 oracle benchmark per ROADMAP Phase 3 'Loop number L=4' diversity axis.  Family layout: 5 massive propagators (l1..l4 squared minus msq, plus a 'wrapping' propagator (l1+l2+l3+l4-p1)^2 - msq gluing the four loops back to the single external leg) and 9 ISPs spanning the remaining l_i.l_j / l_i.p1 scalar products.

cpp_sampled_status.result: completed and matches Mathematica reference at rel ~7.2 × 10⁻³¹ (real) / 1.6 × 10⁻³⁰ (imag).  Audit divergence D7 (the dual-Kira-call master-count mismatch that originally blocked this bench) was fixed in the same session by restructuring `ibp::reduce` and `ibp::diffeq` to mirror upstream `BlackBoxReduce` / `BlackBoxDiffeq` precisely: a Masters-mode preheat call (sector-wide enumeration via `select_mandatory_recursively`) followed by a Reduce-mode call (`select_mandatory_list` for the specific targets), both at the same `(rank, dot)`.  Upstream MMA shares one `$ReductionDirectory` between the two Kira calls; our Kira 2.x release rejects that pattern because the Masters-mode `run_initiate: masters` doesn't register the `-s` numeric substitutions and the subsequent Reduce-mode call sees a stale auxiliary-file state.  We therefore run the two calls in separate subdirectories (`masters_preheat/` and `target_reduce/`) at the same `(rank, dot)` and bridge them with the SubsetQ check mirroring upstream's `If[!SubsetQ[masters, str], Abort]`.  See `src/ibp/reduce.cpp` `reduce` and `diffeq` for the implementation.
cpp_sampled_status.note: C++ output for j[banana4, 1,1,1,1,1,...] = [2507168199924.38622902410513005 +/- 1.82e-18] + i[2.66099952327423468516549716536e-57 +/- 4.37e-87]; matches MMA to ~30 digits in re (well within the project's standard ~10⁻³⁰ oracle tolerance) and to the printed precision in im.  Compare via tools/bench/compare_sampled.py.  Wallclock 399 s, comparable to MMA's 385 s.  The 545 pre-existing tests all remain green after the D7 fix (no regression on the 12 v1.0 oracles).
